title: Only 10% Can Pass This Grammar Quiz
summary: Broken sentences, punctuation traps and almost-correct wording test whether any mistake can slip past you.

landing.intro: Think your grammar is flawless? Repair broken sentences, catch tiny punctuation traps and prove you can spot the mistake before it catches you.

about.body:
This worldwide grammar quiz condenses practical editing into five increasingly difficult rounds and 40 questions. It covers sentence structure, verb forms, punctuation, pronoun clarity, modifier placement and the judgement needed to improve real notices and short documents.

The challenge tests grammar shared across major standard-English varieties. It avoids spelling differences, optional punctuation styles, dialect traps and constructions where respected authorities accept more than one form, so every scored answer follows from the wording and register shown on screen.

Your final percentage reflects only the answers selected in this entertainment challenge. It is a playful snapshot of the language patterns you recognised most confidently, not a formal measure of English proficiency, education or professional editing ability.

howToPlay.title: How to Play
steps: Answer 40 varied proofreading questions across five increasingly difficult rounds.
Correct answers stay hidden while you play, so inspect every verb, reference and punctuation mark before the test moves on.
Finish the challenge to reveal your Grammar Score, strongest skill and complete result report.

about.disclaimer: For entertainment and general learning only. This quiz is not a formal English-language assessment, academic qualification or proof of language proficiency.

checkpoint.finalAdNote: Short ad first — then see your result.

stage-1.preAdCopy: Good start. The next edit gets tougher.

stage-5.preAdCopy: Your grammar score is ready to reveal.

profile-1.title: The Master Editor
profile-1.copy: You handled structure, reference and tiny punctuation details with exceptional control. Even the final multi-clue edits rarely disturbed your command of the page.

profile-2.title: The Natural Grammarian
profile-2.copy: You recognised how sentences fit together and caught most of the challenge’s nearly invisible errors. Your judgement stayed reliable as the material moved from isolated lines to real editing contexts.

profile-3.title: The Sentence Specialist
profile-3.copy: You solved a strong majority of the proofreading problems and adapted well when the format changed. A few fine distinctions kept the final result interesting.

profile-4.title: The Careful Communicator
profile-4.copy: You have a dependable grasp of everyday grammar and a clear eye for several important editing patterns. Your strongest skill shows where that language instinct becomes most confident.

profile-5.title: The Language Improver
profile-5.copy: You caught a solid share of the errors and kept adjusting as the challenge became more demanding. The review will show which patterns are ready to become second nature.

profile-6.title: The Grammar Detective
profile-6.copy: The challenge found some well-hidden traps, but it also revealed the language clues you already notice naturally. Every missed answer is a useful pattern to recognise next time.

insights.overview: Your grammar score at a glance

grammar-r2q3.question: Although the rain stopped ___ the path remained slippery. What belongs in the gap?

grammar-r10q1.question: Which sentence has correct subject–verb agreement?
answers: The list of ingredients are on the counter.
The list of ingredients is on the counter.
The list of ingredients have been placed on the counter.
The list of ingredients were left beside the sink.

grammar-r1q1.question: Which option is a complete sentence?
answers: After the final paragraph
The editor checked the final paragraph.
Because the deadline changed
While everyone was waiting

grammar-r1q3.context: The notes belong to several students.
grammar-r1q3.question: Which sentence uses the apostrophe correctly?
answers: The students’ notes were organised.
The student’s notes were organised.
The students notes’ were organised.
The students note’s were organised.

grammar-r1q4.context: Nora thanked Priya after Priya corrected the caption.
grammar-r1q4.question: Which revision makes the reference clearest?
answers: Nora thanked her after she corrected it.
She thanked Priya after she corrected it.
Nora thanked Priya for correcting the caption.
Nora thanked Priya after it was corrected by her.

grammar-r1q5.question: Which wording is the clearest and most concise?
answers: The report is concise in a clear manner.
The report is concise and clear.
The report has clarity and is concise in nature.
The report is being of a concise and clear kind.

grammar-r1q6.context: FORMAL NOTICE: Visitors must report to reception before entering the studio.
grammar-r1q6.question: Which version is clearest for the notice?
answers: Visitors, maybe report before entering.
Before entering it, reception is where visitors report.
Visitors report, to reception before entering the studio.
Before entering the studio, visitors must report to reception.

grammar-r2q5.context: The sentence describes two actions completed yesterday.
grammar-r2q5.question: Which sentence keeps the verb forms consistent?
answers: Mina opens the file and checked the figures.
Mina had opened the file and checks the figures.
Mina opened the file and checked the figures.
Mina opening the file and checked the figures.

grammar-r3q1.question: The meeting began at 09:00. Leo finished the chart at 08:30. Which sentence is correct?
answers: Leo completed the chart after the meeting began.
Leo had completed the chart after the meeting began.
Leo has completed the chart before the meeting began.
Leo had completed the chart before the meeting began.

grammar-r4q3.question: Which sentence uses a semicolon correctly?
answers: The file was large; because it loaded slowly.
The file was large; it loaded slowly.
The file was large, it loaded slowly.
The file was large; although it loaded slowly.

grammar-r3q2.context: Asha started at the library on Monday and still works there now.
grammar-r3q2.question: Which sentence matches the timeline?
answers: Asha worked at the library since Monday.
Asha has worked at the library since Monday.
Asha had worked at the library since Monday, but still does.
Asha is work at the library since Monday.

grammar-r3q5.context: The clause “which won the award” must describe the documentary, not the director.
grammar-r3q5.question: Which sentence attaches the clause clearly?
answers: The director, which won the award, introduced the documentary.
The director introduced, which won the award, the documentary.
Which won the award, the director introduced the documentary.
The director introduced the documentary, which won the award.

grammar-r3q6.question: Which sentence uses a reflexive pronoun correctly?
answers: The technicians completed the review by theirselves.
The technicians completed the review by themselves.
The technicians completed the review by themself.
The technicians completed themselves the review.

grammar-r4q1.question: Which sentence introduces the list correctly?
answers: Bring three items: a notebook, a pen and identification.
Bring: three items a notebook, a pen and identification.
Bring three: items, a notebook a pen and identification.
Bring three items; a notebook, a pen and identification.

grammar-r4q5.context: Maya was walking into the room when she noticed the open window.
grammar-r4q5.question: Which sentence places the opening modifier clearly?
answers: Walking into the room, Maya noticed the open window.
Walking into the room, the open window caught Maya’s attention.
Maya noticed, walking into the room, the open window.
The room walking in, Maya noticed the window.

grammar-r4q6.context:
NOTICE
For a clear formal notice, greet the host, sign the register and collect a badge.
grammar-r4q6.question: Which version is punctuated correctly?
answers: Greet the host sign the register, and collect a badge.
Greet, the host, sign the register and collect a badge.
Greet the host, sign the register and collect a badge.
Greet the host; sign the register, and collect a badge because.

grammar-r5q4.context: Between Lina and ___, this decision must remain confidential.
grammar-r5q4.question: Which pronoun correctly completes the sentence?
answers: me
I
my
mine

grammar-r10q4.question: Several chefs share these lockers. Which sign is written correctly?
answers: The chefs lockers
The chef's lockers
The chefs' lockers
The chefs's lockers

grammar-r5q1.context: The policy has two sections. The second section contains the deadline.
grammar-r5q1.question: Which revision refers to the deadline most clearly?
answers: It contains it in the second one.
The policy has two sections, and it contains the deadline.
The deadline appears in the policy’s second section.
The second has it, which is in the policy.

grammar-r5q5.question: Which option is a complete, correctly ordered sentence?
answers: Because the labels were missing.
The labels, because missing, the boxes.
The boxes were delayed because the labels were missing.
The boxes because the labels were missing delayed.

grammar-r5q6.question: Which sentence correctly punctuates a direct address?
answers: Ravi please, check the final line.
Ravi, please check the final line.
Ravi please check, the final line.
Ravi; please, check the final line.

grammar-r6q1.context: Only the blue folders were archived; the other folders remained active.
grammar-r6q1.question: Which sentence preserves that restriction?
answers: The folders were archived blue only.
Only the folders were archived in blue.
The folders only were archived blue.
Only the blue folders were archived.

grammar-r6q5.question: Which sentence has correct agreement?
answers: The set of instructions are easy to follow.
The set of instructions were easy to follow now.
The set of instructions be easy to follow.
The set of instructions is easy to follow.

grammar-r6q6.context: EMAIL GOAL: Ask the team to submit one final file by 17:00.
grammar-r6q6.question: Which sentence is clearest?
answers: Please submit the final file by 17:00.
Please, submit finally the file somewhere around 17:00 maybe.
The final file should have submission by the team in a final way.
By 17:00, a file final the team submits please.

grammar-r10q5.question: Which notice is grammatically correct?
answers: Visitors must sign in, wearing a badge and return it before leaving.
Visitors must sign in, wear a badge and return it before leaving.
Visitors must sign in, wear a badge and returning it before leaving.
Visitors must sign in, to wear a badge and return it before leaving.

grammar-r9q5.question: Only the first report was revised. Which sentence makes that meaning unambiguous?
answers: Only the editor revised the first report.
The editor revised the first report only to correct the title.
The editor revised the first report only yesterday.
The editor revised only the first report.
trapdoorErrors: only changes who performed the action
the purpose phrase changes why the report was revised
only changes when the action happened

grammar-r7q3.context:
PARAGRAPH
The room was ready. Except for the missing chairs. The guests arrived at noon.
grammar-r7q3.question: Which edit removes the fragment?
answers: The room was ready except for the missing chairs. The guests arrived at noon.
The room was ready. Except the missing chairs were. The guests arrived.
The room. Was ready except for missing chairs, guests arrived.
Except for the missing chairs. The room was ready and at noon.

grammar-r7q4.context: The intended meaning is that the speaker answered nearly every question.
grammar-r7q4.question: Which wording expresses that meaning?
answers: The speaker answered every nearly question.
Nearly the speaker answered every question.
The speaker nearly answered every question.
The speaker answered nearly every question.

grammar-r7q5.context: The second clause explains the first.
grammar-r7q5.question: Which punctuation is correct?
answers: The deadline moved; because the client requested more time.
The deadline moved: the client requested more time.
The deadline: moved the client requested more time.
The deadline moved, the client requested more time.

grammar-r7q6.context: A report contains a summary and an appendix. The appendix is updated monthly.
grammar-r7q6.question: Which edit makes the monthly update refer to the appendix?
answers: The report contains a summary and an appendix, and it is updated monthly.
It contains a summary and an appendix that is updated monthly by it.
The report contains a summary and an appendix; the appendix is updated monthly.
The report, updated monthly, contains a summary and its appendix.

grammar-r9q1.question: Which sentence handles the contrast correctly?
answers: The storm ended; although the streets remained flooded.
The storm ended, however the streets remained flooded.
Although the storm ended; the streets remained flooded.
Although the storm ended, the streets remained flooded.
trapdoorErrors: semicolon incorrectly separates a main clause from a dependent clause
conjunctive adverb lacks the required boundary punctuation
semicolon incorrectly follows a dependent clause

grammar-r9q2.context:
STATUS
One final title is ready. Three revised captions are also ready.
grammar-r9q2.question: Which sentence has correct agreement?
answers: Three revised captions, as well as the final title, is ready.
Three revised captions, as well as the final title, be ready.
Three revised captions, as well as the final title, are ready.
Three revised captions, as well as the final title, being ready.
trapdoorErrors: singular verb does not agree with the plural subject
base form cannot stand alone as the finite verb
non-finite form leaves the sentence incomplete

visual.ariaLabel: The final reports were checked before the editor approve them

grammar-r7q2.question: Which numbered part contains the error?
answers: A
B
C
D

grammar-r10q6.question: Which sentence is completely correct?
answers: After reviewing the figures, Maya confirmed that each total was accurate.
After reviewing the figures, each total was confirmed by Maya.
After reviewing the figures Maya confirmed that each total was accurate.
After reviewing the figures, Maya confirmed that each of the totals were accurate.

grammar-r8q1.question: Choose the correct coordination.
answers: The doors opened, but nobody entered.
The doors opened, nobody entered.
Although the doors opened, but nobody entered.
The doors opened but. Nobody entered.

grammar-r8q3.context: The handle belongs to one door.
grammar-r8q3.question: Choose the correct apostrophe.
answers: the doors handle
the doors’ handle
the door’s handle
the door’ handle

grammar-r8q4.question: Choose the reflexive pronoun.
answers: The designers prepared the display by theirselves.
The designers prepared the display by themselves.
The designers prepared the display by themself.
The designers prepared the display by theirs.

grammar-r8q5.context: The number almost doubled but did not quite reach twice its original size.
grammar-r8q5.question: Which wording matches?
answers: The update nearly doubled the number.
The update doubled nearly the number.
Nearly the update doubled the number.
The update doubled the nearly number.

grammar-r8q6.question: Which formal edit works?
answers: Send it soon-ish.
The file, send whenever.
Sending of file is wanted.
Please send the file by noon.

grammar-r10q2.context:
TIMELINE
10:00 — the team completed the checks.
10:30 — the doors opened.
The account is written from 11:00.
grammar-r10q2.question: Which sentence reports the order correctly?
answers: The team had completed the checks before the doors opened.
The team completes the checks after the doors opened.
The team has complete the checks before the doors open yesterday.
The team were completed the checks after opening.
